title: Preservation by total-limit completed strict-system pullback
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite extension E/Q_ell and a finite-field datum D [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let f:X->Y be a separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type D.k-schemes. Let S be any specified derived-system calculus on Y [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. For an integral bounded constructible P on Y [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], form N=f^* S.reduction(P) with the actual strict-system inverse image [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and F=L_X N with the actual total derived limit. Then F is integral bounded constructible, N is normalized, and for every ordered integer interval [a,b], if every finite reduction of P has Tor amplitude [a,b], every finite reduction of F has Tor amplitude [a,b] [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. No dual or exceptional operation is involved.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9(4)-(5), printed pp. 50-51, completed inverse image and preservation; parent DAG proof steps 2-4.

proof.text: The DVR and completeness of the extension-integer ring verify the coefficient-system inverse-image hypotheses: a uniformizer is a non-zero-divisor and the ring equals the inverse limit of its powers quotients. Exact system pullback commutes with derived quotient extension. Its transition adjunct at m>=n is finite pullback of the reduction system transition adjunct, conjugated by the quotient tensor comparison; hence it is invertible. Thus N is normalized.

On a single flat-term K-flat representative, the strict reduction tower, finite inverse image, and the total limit give the Roos construction defining integralDerivedPullback. Its resolving-class descent comparison identifies F with that completed pullback. The integral preservation theorem makes F constructible.

Normalized reconstruction makes the actual counit R_X F -> N invertible. Its finite evaluations composed with reductionEvaluation and the inverse-image evaluation comparison identify each reduction of F with finite inverse image of the corresponding reduction of P. Finite pullback preserves precisely [a,b], so transport the Tor amplitude through these isomorphisms.

theorem completedSystemPullbackPreservation
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [IsSeparated (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [f.IsOver (Spec (.of D.k))] [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (S : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E Y)
    (P : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E Y) :
    let N := (integralComparisonDerivedSequencePullback l E f).obj (S.reduction.obj P.obj)
    let F := (coefficientSequenceLimit l E X).obj N
    sfIntegralConstructible l E X F ∧ IsNormalizedCoefficientSequence l E X N ∧
      (∀ (a b : ℤ), a ≤ b →
        (∀ n : ℕ, HasProEtaleTorAmplitude Y (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1))
          ((scalarReductionDerivedExtension l E Y n).obj P.obj) a b) →
        ∀ n : ℕ, HasProEtaleTorAmplitude X (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1))
          ((scalarReductionDerivedExtension l E X n).obj F) a b)
